subject: SaaSCo security questionnaire: regional access, retention, and deletion (hosted API)
messages:
From: Claire Wallace <claire.wallace@saasco.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@saasco.com
Date: 2028-07-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regional residency + retention details for hosted API

Hi Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to answer a few items for our security questionnaire. We need concise, authoritative responses we can share with our legal and cloud teams. Our main asks are:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that request content and generated responses for tenant SaaSCo will remain in the EU for the hosted API option? If so, please explain the controls and whether backups/snapshots may be outside the region.

2) What is the default retention period for request payloads, response content, and derived logs (e.g., usage metrics, error traces)? How can we shorten that for compliance reasons?

3) What is your deletion workflow and SLA when we request an account-wide erasure (including backups and logs)? Any exceptions (legal hold, fraud investigation) to note?

4) Are there technical controls customers can use to minimize persistent storage of PII (e.g., tokenization headers, ephemeral-only mode)?

Please include links to documentation and any downloadable artifacts we can attach to our security review.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Pacific.

Best,
Claire Wallace
Security & Privacy Program
SaaSCo

From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Claire Wallace <claire.wallace@saasco.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, security@saasco.com
Date: 2028-07-19T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional residency + retention details for hosted API

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise, actionable answers you can paste into the questionnaire. I copied Marissa (Account Lead) for visibility and to help coordinate any SLA paperwork.

1) Regional residency (EU):
- Short answer: yes — for hosted API customers selecting the EU tenancy, full request/response processing and primary storage are confined to EU-hosted regions.
- Controls: tenant routing pins traffic to EU data centers, encryption-at-rest using region-specific KMS keys, and strict IAM scoping so platform operators managing the EU tenancy have background access controls scoped to EU operations.
- Backups/snapshots: primary backups are taken in-region. Disaster recovery replicates encrypted snapshots to a secondary EU site. We do not replicate customer request/response data outside the EU for hosted-api customers who select EU residency.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response content: default retention is 30 days for hosted API (used for billing reconciliation, abuse monitoring, and model quality diagnostics). Data is encrypted at rest and access is limited to authorized roles.
- Derived logs & metrics (aggregated usage metrics, latency traces): retained for up to 180 days for operational troubleshooting and capacity planning.
- Audit logs (admin actions, auth events): retained for 365 days by default.
- Shortening retention: Enterprise customers can request reduced retention windows (example: 7 days for request/response) by filing a configuration change during onboarding. We also offer an add-on for zero-retention (no storage of request/response payloads) when paired with dedicated auditing hooks and contractual terms.

3) Deletion workflow and SLA:
- Workflow: customer submits an account erasure request via the Console or via security@redwoodinference.com. We validate the request with account owner information, schedule a deletion job that: (a) removes primary data stores, (b) purges caches/KV prefixes, (c) flags records in analytics pipelines to exclude from future aggregates, and (d) schedules removal from backups as part of the next backup lifecycle pass.
- SLA: standard hosted API erasure window is 30 calendar days end-to-end from validated request. Enterprise plans can contract for accelerated erasure (7–14 days) as part of onboarding.
- Exceptions: we will not delete data subject to a lawful hold, subpoena, or active fraud/abuse investigation. Any such exception will be communicated with the requesting admin and logged in the audit trail.

4) Technical controls to minimize persisted PII:
- Ephemeral mode: customers can opt into 'ephemeral mode' (request header X-Redwood-Ephemeral: true) that disables storage of request/response artifacts — useful for single-call lookups. Ephemeral requests are excluded from billing-level sampling used for model quality diagnostics (and billed slightly differently).
- Client-side tokenization: recommend client-side pseudonymization where feasible; we support structured response schemas and token placeholders to avoid storing raw PII.
- KMS scoping & customer-managed keys: EU customers can bring their own KMS keys to control encryption lifecycle.

References and artifacts included below. If you need contract language for the SaaS agreement (data processing addendum, deletion SLA clauses), Marissa can route that to Legal.

Links: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api-data-retention | https://redwood.ai/docs/ephemeral-mode

Irene Choi
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

Claire — quick answers inline and a suggested contract snippet below. Marissa will follow up to schedule a DPA review.

1) Accelerated erasure SLA contract wording (suggested):
"Upon receipt of a validated account erasure request submitted by Customer’s authorized administrator, Redwood Inference will complete deletion of Customer Data (including primary stores, caches, and scheduled removal from backups) within fourteen (14) calendar days. For customers who have contracted an accelerated erasure addendum, that period will be seven (7) calendar days. Exceptions apply for data subject to lawful hold or ongoing fraud investigation, in which case Redwood will notify Customer and preserve relevant records only to the extent required by law."

2) Ephemeral mode limitations:
- Supported: normal text generation, embeddings, and standard function-calling.
- Limitations: long-running streaming sessions that rely on token-level diagnostics may be restricted; ephemeral mode disables model-quality sampling of request content (so some logging-based diagnostics are unavailable). Third-party tools requiring stored context (e.g., multi-turn cross-request context stored on our side) are incompatible unless the customer opts into a short retention window.

Next steps: Marissa will share the DPA and addendum PDF and propose a 30-minute review slot. If you want the contract snippet adjusted to your legal language, we can provide an editable redline.

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
